books.section: Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

stimulus.source_note: Original secondary passage written for this question; facts from the grounding books.
stimulus.text: Clay's plan first went to the Senate as one large bill, the Omnibus Bill, meant to be voted on all at once. It failed in the Senate in July 1850: Northerners who liked California's admission would not vote for the Fugitive Slave Act, and Southerners who wanted that act would not vote for California. President Zachary Taylor, who opposed the package, died on July 9, 1850, and Millard Fillmore, who favored it, became president. Senator Stephen A. Douglas of Illinois then broke the package into five separate bills, and each one passed with a different mix of Northern and Southern votes. Fillmore signed all five between September 9 and September 20, 1850.

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note
stem: The passage best supports which conclusion about the Compromise of 1850 as a whole?

options.text: It settled the slavery question so completely that no one challenged it again.
options.misconception: Background from the books: the compromise was challenged within four years — the Kansas-Nebraska Act of 1854 reopened the territorial question the compromise had postponed.

options.text: It passed only by breaking the bargain apart, leaving each side a prize.
It failed to pass Congress, and California stayed a territory for another decade.
options.misconception: All five bills passed and Fillmore signed them between September 9 and September 20, 1850; California became a state that year.

options.text: It was imposed on Congress by President Taylor over the Senate's objections.
options.misconception: Taylor opposed the package and died before it passed; it was Fillmore, his successor, who signed the bills.

rationales.A: Background from the books: the compromise was challenged within four years — the Kansas-Nebraska Act of 1854 reopened the territorial question the compromise had postponed.
rationales.B: Each bill passed with a different mix of votes, so no majority ever endorsed the whole bargain. Background from the books: the North got California while the South got the Fugitive Slave Act, and each side resented the other's prize.
rationales.C: All five bills passed and Fillmore signed them between September 9 and September 20, 1850; California became a state that year.
rationales.D: Taylor opposed the package and died before it passed; it was Fillmore, his successor, who signed the bills.
rationales.general:
1. Ask what never happened: no single vote ever approved the whole compromise together.
2. Count the real votes instead: five bills, five different majorities, each built from different friends.
3. Background from the books: each side celebrated its own prize while resenting the other's.
Remember: a deal nobody voted for as a whole is a deal held together by habit, not by agreement.
